recoveryStepTitleBank.message: Call your bank on the number printed on your card

recoveryStepTitleChangePassword.message: Change the password you typed, and anywhere else you used it

recoveryStepTitleDisconnect.message: Disconnect this device from the network

recoveryStepTitlePasswordsElsewhere.message: Change your email password from a different device

recoveryStepTitleRemoteAccess.message: Remove any remote-access software they had you install

recoveryStepTitleScan.message: Run a full scan with your system’s own security tool

recoveryStepTitleSessions.message: Sign out of all sessions on your important accounts

recoveryStepWhyBank.message: Not the number you were given. If money moved, the earlier they know, the more of it can be stopped.

recoveryStepWhyChangePassword.message: A password entered on a fake site is tried immediately on every service that shares it.

recoveryStepWhyDisconnect.message: Anything already running loses its connection to whoever placed it, which stops the theft while you work through the rest.

recoveryStepWhyPasswordsElsewhere.message: Email is the key to every other account. Changing it from the affected device would hand the new password over too.

recoveryStepWhyRemoteAccess.message: That software is how they get back in, and it keeps working long after the call ends.

recoveryStepWhyScan.message: It looks for what the command installed. Do this after the accounts are safe, not before — the accounts are what an attacker uses first.

recoveryStepWhySessions.message: A stolen session cookie keeps working after a password change until the session itself is ended.

recoveryStepWhyTwoFactor.message: Adding a second factor of their own is how an intruder keeps access after you have locked them out.

recoveryStepWhyWatch.message: Access that survives everything above shows up as a login you do not recognise.
